newsitem.title: GERMANY: Buba faces no new need to cut rates-economists.
newsitem.headline: Buba faces no new need to cut rates-economists.

text.p: Germany faces no pressing need to adjust its interest rates and the Bundesbank is likely to keep its three main rates steady this week, pushing out the timing of an easing that many economists still expect in 1997.

In a Reuters poll, 10 economists unanimously forecast the central bank's policy-making council would vote to keep the discount and Lombard rates at 2.50 and 4.50 percent respectively at Thursday's regular scheduled meeting.
They also predicted Germany's main money market rate, the repo, would again be fixed at three percent, the rate which has prevailed since late August.

"There is no reason for a change," said Steven King, economist at James Capel in London, echoing a common sentiment that nothing had changed since the German central bank left rates steady two weeks ago.

Not even much weaker than expected December manufacturing orders, which fell 1.4 percent, were seen as enough to convince the central bank that another rate cut was either necessary or even capable of breathing new life into the economy.

Stressing that such data was often revised significantly, Klaus Holschuh, head of bonds research at Commerzbank in Frankfurt, said neither Wednesday's weak orders data nor Tuesday's strong output data "signalled a change in the trend".
